description: Dassault Mirage F1CZ serial 207. Spent roughly twenty years at the University of Stellenbosch Department of Mechanical Engineering before being donated to the Stellenbosch Flying Club; moved after eighteen months of planning with Paramount Group supplying a hydraulic bolt puller and a fuselage lifting frame. Reported by defenceWeb on 5 June 2019 as a permanent display; the aircraft has no engine and there are no plans to make it airworthy. Confirmed again as club property on display in a defenceWeb gate-guard survey of 26 February 2020. TAIL NUMBER DELIBERATELY BLANK: the SAAF serial is 207 and is not in doubt, but the database enforces a unique key on model plus tail number and a French Armee de l Air Mirage F1C-200 also serialled 207 is already recorded at the Musee de l Air et de l Espace. The SAAF serial is preserved in the aliases.

de Havilland Vampire FB.52, serial 241, unveiled at Stellenbosch Flying Club on 18 November 2006 after a volunteer restoration. By November 2011 a club member reported her weathered and canopy-damaged by a collapsed metal pole and began a fresh clean-up effort. Still recorded as present in a defenceWeb survey of 26 February 2020, which notes the Vampire at Stellenbosch remains on SAAF Museum inventory rather than club property. Condition in 2026 unverified.

Ex-RAF Lightning F6, civil-registered ZU-BEW in South Africa and flown by Thunder City at Cape Town International, including a display at the Stellenbosch airshow in March 2003. After Thunder City ceased operating the other Lightnings were sold for export; XR773 was offered to the SAAF Museum, which declined it because it never served in South Africa, and was instead donated to Stellenbosch Flying Club. Moved to Stellenbosch on 11 September 2023 for reassembly and refurbishment as a static display; as of October 2024 no completion had been reported.
